Led
lĕd
v. (past tense and past participle of lead; rendering Hebrew nahah and yalak, Greek ago)
Old English lædan, to cause to go; the past form of lead. The word of a hand upon the way — someone else chose the road.

Biblical Definition

To be led is to be brought along a way by another. God led Israel by the pillar and not by the short road: “God led the people about, through the way of the wilderness” (Exo 13:18), and “led thee these forty years in the wilderness, to humble thee, and to prove thee” (Deu 8:2). Christ was “led up of the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted” (Mat 4:1) and “led as a sheep to the slaughter” (Act 8:32). The Christian is defined by the same passive: “as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God” (Rom 8:14); “if ye be led of the Spirit, ye are not under the law” (Gal 5:18). The ascended Christ “led captivity captive, and gave gifts unto men” (Eph 4:8).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) gives led as the past tense and participle of lead: conducted, guided, drawn.

expand to see more

LED, pret. and pp. of lead. Conducted; guided; drawn; allured.

Key Scripture

Rom 8:14 — "For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God."

Gal 5:18 — "But if ye be led of the Spirit, ye are not under the law."

Deu 8:2 — "And thou shalt remember all the way which the LORD thy God led thee these forty years in the wilderness, to humble thee, and to prove thee, to know what was in thine heart, whether thou wouldest keep his commandments, or no."

Act 8:32 — "The place of the scripture which he read was this, He was led as a sheep to the slaughter; and like a lamb dumb before his shearer, so opened he not his mouth:"

Eph 4:8 — "Wherefore he saith, When he ascended up on high, he led captivity captive, and gave gifts unto men."

Exo 13:18 — "But God led the people about, through the way of the wilderness of the Red sea: and the children of Israel went up harnessed out of the land of Egypt."

Modern Corruption

Being led by the Spirit is claimed for private impressions, and Paul uses the phrase for the mortifying of sin.

expand to see more

Romans 8:14 stands at the end of an argument, not at the start of a mystery. The verse before it reads, “if ye through the Spirit do mortify the deeds of the body, ye shall live,” and then: “For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God.” The leading Paul has in view is visible in a killed sin, not felt in an inward nudge. Galatians 5:18 does the same work — “if ye be led of the Spirit, ye are not under the law” — and the sentence runs straight on into the works of the flesh and the fruit of the Spirit. Being led has a direction, and the direction is holiness. The man who says the Spirit led him into what Scripture forbids has named the wrong leader.

The passive voice is the point of the word. Christ was led to the slaughter; Israel was led through the wilderness; and every one of the forty years was chosen for them, “to humble thee, and to prove thee, to know what was in thine heart.” Exodus 13:17 records that God led them not through the way of the land of the Philistines, “although that was near,” lest the people repent when they saw war. The direct road was refused on purpose. Those who complain that God's path is indirect have Exodus 13 against them: the short way was the way that would have destroyed them.

Ephesians 4:8 turns the word to triumph. Psalm 68 pictured a conqueror ascending with his captives in train; Paul says the ascended Christ “led captivity captive” — the captor taken captive — and distributed the spoil as gifts to the church. The One who was led away bound to Caiaphas (Mat 26:57) and led away to be crucified (John 19:16) is the same One who now leads the whole procession.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew nahah (H5148), to guide; yalak in the causative (H3212), to cause to walk; Greek ago (G71), to lead, bring; aichmaloteuo (G162), to lead captive.

expand to see more

Hebrew nahah (H5148) — to lead, guide; Exodus 13:17, 13:21, Psalm 23:3, Psalm 78:14.

Hebrew yalak, hiphil (H3212) — to cause to go, to lead; Deuteronomy 8:2, 8:15, 29:5.

Greek ago (G71) — to lead, bring, carry; Luke 4:1, Acts 8:32, Romans 8:14, Galatians 5:18.

Greek aichmaloteuo (G162) — to lead captive; Ephesians 4:8, quoting Psalm 68:18.

Usage

"“As many as are led by the Spirit of God” — sonship shown in the leading, and the leading shown in a mortified sin."

"“He led captivity captive” — the Ascension as a triumph."

"“He was led as a sheep to the slaughter” — Isaiah 53 read aloud in a chariot."
